description: This 2015 technical report by Carol Lee Roalkvam for the Federal Highway Administration documents a climate resilience pilot in which the Washington State Department of Transportation worked with federal agencies to make highways in the Skagit River Basin more resilient to flooding. The team combined WSDOT's own vulnerability assessment data with the flood analysis of the US Army Corps of Engineers' Skagit River Flood Risk Management investigation, and used the results to inform transportation asset management, reveal vulnerable assets that had not been recognised and identify adaptation strategies. It adds recommendations and lessons on coordination across jurisdictions and sectors. Coverage is one river basin in Washington State. The report is a PDF of about 15 MB on the ROSA P repository, free to download, with no licence stated. Caveats: only the abstract page was read, findings are qualitative and the flood models and data are those of the cited studies. For simulation, it is a documented use of flood hazard exposure and resilience analysis for road assets and adaptation planning. No closely related catalogue record was identified in this pass.
